## Context / Problem

RP-04's config-ownership drain reaches its final two rows. After C3f
(`ed65`) drains the nine residual files, `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py`
`LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` holds exactly TWO rows, both on
`_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_lifecycle.py`:

- `RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` — the consecutive-404 absence-retire grace,
  read in `note_absent` via the local `_env_int` shim.
- `os.environ.get` — the raw ambient lookup inside that same `_env_int` parser.

Both were MOVED into `binding_lifecycle.py` from `binding_store.py` by RP-02 S2
(the absence policy travelled with them). RP-04 S7.3.a (ticket `6633`) closed
having cut the reconciler CORE/JIRA reads but NOT these — its recorded file
impact named the pre-move `binding_store.py`, so the moved reads fell through.
Tracker `01d8` records the coupling but is bookkeeping-only (no file impact,
out of the epic tree). This story is the executable drain that RP-02 S2's move
left owing, and it is the LAST one before the whitelist is EMPTY.

## Key finding — the owned accessor already exists

The cut is NOT a constructor-threading refactor. `src/rebar/_config_sources.py`
(a composition root that owns env reads) ALREADY exposes
`resolve_absent_retire_grace()` — "Owns the read for binding_store/binding_walk"
— with byte-identical semantics to the local shim: raw `RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE`
over the default `3`, clamped `>= 1`, malformed/absent → default. The sibling
reconciler knobs in `fetcher.py`/`applier.py` were cut to `_config_sources`
accessors the same way (they now carry no ambient reads and no whitelist rows),
so this is the established, in-process pattern.

## Approach

1. In `binding_lifecycle.py::note_absent`, replace the
   `_env_int("RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE", _DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE, minimum=1)`
   call with `resolve_absent_retire_grace()` imported from `rebar._config_sources`
   (the same import direction `fetcher.py`/`applier.py` already use — no cycle).
2. Remove the now-dead `_env_int` helper and the local
   `_DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` constant from `binding_lifecycle.py` (confirm no
   other caller first), eliminating the ambient `os.environ.get` read entirely.
3. Remove BOTH `binding_lifecycle.py` rows from
   `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py`. `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` is now EMPTY.

## Portability

The cut composes through an in-process owned accessor
(`_config_sources.resolve_absent_retire_grace`); it has no CI-provider or
external-service trigger. The config-ownership gate is a deterministic offline
AST check. Works with any or no CI provider.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `note_absent`'s absence-retire grace is sourced from
  `_config_sources.resolve_absent_retire_grace()`; no ambient `os.environ` read
  or `_env_int`-style shim for it remains below the seam in `binding_lifecycle.py`.
- [ ] The dead `_env_int` helper is removed (no remaining caller), so
  `binding_lifecycle.py` carries zero below-seam config/credential reads.
- [ ] Both `binding_lifecycle.py` rows are removed from
  `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py`, and `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` is now
  EMPTY (`[]`) — the whole-tree config-ownership drain is complete.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` reports zero findings with the
  whitelist empty.
- [ ] Absence-retire behavior is byte-preserved: default 3, clamp `>= 1`,
  malformed/absent env → default; a set valid value is honored; a binding
  retires at exactly `grace` consecutive 404s.

## Testing / Verification

- Held-out oracle (RED-first before the cut): `python -m pytest
  tests/scripts/test_binding_lifecycle_grace_seam_clean_heldout.py -q` — asserts
  `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS == []`, the gate is clean for `binding_lifecycle.py`, no
  `_env_int` shim remains, and the grace behavior is byte-preserved.
- Config-ownership gate: `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` (exit 0).
- Module-size gate: `find src/rebar -name '*.py' | grep -v __pycache__ |
  xargs wc -l | awk '$2!="total" && $1>800'` (empty).
- Env-registry drift: `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check` (clean).
- Full pre-flight: `make lint && make typecheck`, plus the reconciler
  binding-lifecycle unit tests (`pytest -k binding`).
